answer: The registry's atlas lists broken devices, each with a serial shared by no second unit. A newcomer draws one device, diagnoses its fault, fits the part, and files a repair fable: a log of fault, fix, and test result, countersigned by an inspector's re-test. Steps unlock only after each filing verifies, so one serial serves one holder. Three verified repairs build a trellis of endorsements granting standing. One identity costs $180 plus 14 bench hours; 5,000 fakes need 5,000 devices, $900,000, 70,000 hours, and no spares warehouse repairs a second serial: each unit needs its hands and re-test.
